title: Widen group-commit window and lower activation threshold on accepted WAL bundle
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 leaves the group-commit window too short to coalesce the 5-terminal commit stream; wal_waiting_backends still hits 1 and wal_sync_time_per_txn is 1.06ms/txn while sync_average_ms is only 0.13ms, indicating queueing rather than slow fsync.
mechanism: The accepted WAL bundle (wal_buffers 2048, wal_writer_delay 20, wal_writer_flush_after 0, wal_compression on) already cut wal_bytes_per_txn 15-19% and raised TPS, but the mechanism verdict was refuted because sync_average_ms did not fall: the remaining cost is commit-path queueing, not per-sync latency. commit_delay=100us is below the observed inter-commit spacing at ~23k TPS, so the window rarely collects siblings. Widening commit_delay to 500us and lowering commit_siblings to 1 makes the collector fire on nearly every commit and batch more fsyncs per group, while keeping wal_writer_flush_after=0 (writer flushes immediately) so pre-flushed WAL is available for the group.
query_effect: No plan change; commit-path only. GetUserTweets p50 (171us) and InsertTweet p50 (387us) should shrink slightly as commit queueing drops.
expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps modestly (>=0.3%) by freeing terminal capacity currently spent waiting on WAL sync.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease wal_sync_time_per_txn and GetUserTweets p95; commit_delay adds at most 500us only when a sibling is present, which is bounded and amortized across the group.

predictions.rationale: Larger group-commit window batches more commits per fsync, lowering sync time per transaction.
Fewer commits queue on WAL flush when siblings are collected into one sync.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.

alternatives.statement: If commit_delay=500us adds latency without collecting siblings (low concurrency), wal_sync_time_per_txn stays flat and GetUserTweets p50 rises.
If the residual WAL wait is fsync device latency rather than queueing, sync_average_ms rises with larger batches and TPS does not improve.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent already holds the accepted WAL bundle but leaves the group-commit collector under-tuned (100us window, threshold 2). Widening the window and lowering the threshold is the direct lever on the still-present wal_wait anomaly without touching already-optimal wal_buffers/wal_compression.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 5x current 100us, within safe [0,1000]; 500us is below observed GetUserTweets p50 171us*? no—chosen to exceed inter-commit spacing at ~23k TPS (~43us) by an order of magnitude while staying under 1ms.
Lower activation threshold from 2 to 1, within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals and ~23k TPS, threshold 1 makes the collector fire on nearly every commit.
Keep at 0 (immediate writer flush) so pre-flushed WAL is available to the widened group-commit window; unchanged value retained for bundle coherence.

nodes.label: Larger group-commit window batches more commits per fsync, reducing commit-path queueing

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: confirm GetUserTweets plan unchanged so TPS gain is attributable to commit path
